text: Although the positives are often overlooked. <break time="0.8s" /> Break ups can actually be extremely beneficial. <break time="0.8s" /> Separation enables people to escape. <break time="0.8s" /> Unfulfilling, negative, and even harmful relationships. <break time="0.8s" /> Promoting feelings of relief, empowerment. <break time="0.8s" /> And excitement about future possibilities. <break time="0.8s" /> Furthermore even when left devastated. <break time="0.8s" /> With a broken heart and shattered dreams. <break time="0.8s" /> All is not lost. <break time="0.8s" /> As individuals are likely to experience growth. <break time="0.8s" /> Tashiro and Frazier found. <break time="0.8s" /> That after the end of a relationship. <break time="0.8s" /> Individuals reported greater self confidence. <break time="0.8s" /> Improvements in communication strategies. <break time="0.8s" /> Better relationships with others. <break time="0.8s" /> And more positive expectations about future relationships. <break time="0.8s" /> As with other significant life events. <break time="0.8s" /> Break ups can act as a catalyst for making big life changes. <break time="0.8s" /> Enabling individuals to grow. <break time="0.8s" /> Beyond their previous level of psychological functioning. <break time="0.8s" /> In sum. <break time="0.8s" /> While relationship breakdowns can clearly be very stressful. <break time="0.8s" /> Maybe it is time to change the narrative. <break time="0.8s" /> Away from the doom and gloom of break ups. <break time="0.8s" /> And, acknowledging that most relationships are finite. <break time="0.8s" /> View separation not just as an end. <break time="0.8s" /> But as a new opportunity to grow and better ourselves.
